description: Reviewed decisions about whether a lesson's Learn It teaches THAT lesson. Hand-maintained; tools/validate-learn-it-scope.mjs reads it. An entry exists for every finding the detectors raise. A finding with no entry has NOT been reviewed, and the validator says so rather than implying otherwise. An entry whose finding no longer fires must be deleted — stale absolutions are worse than no file.

classifications.ALIGNED: Learn It prepares students for this lesson's source task. The finding is a naming difference, not a scope problem.
classifications.SUPPORTING: The concept is prerequisite or access vocabulary the lesson genuinely leans on, not new instruction.
classifications.OVER-BROAD: Learn It introduces a unit concept students do not need yet. Corrected.
classifications.OFF-TARGET: Learn It teaches a different concept from the lesson objective. Corrected.
classifications.PREMATURE: Learn It teaches mathematics a later lesson owns. Corrected or moved to an extension.
classifications.MISSING: Learn It failed to explain something the source task requires. Corrected.

reviewed.subject: math story
reviewed.reason: The Learn It card is titled 'We are all doers of math' and its opening question — 'where does math already live in your day?' — IS the math story prompt. The objective names the artifact, the card asks for it in student language.

reviewed.subject: persevere
reviewed.reason: Taught in plain language rather than by name: the key idea says students 'try other strategies when we come to dead ends', which is perseverance stated for a sixth grader. Keeping the term gives the behaviour a name to point at.

reviewed.subject: Data distribution
reviewed.reason: The median is introduced as the middle of an ordered set, which is a statement about the distribution. The term is Unit 2 vocabulary students meet across several lessons rather than instruction this lesson adds.

reviewed.subject: Variability
reviewed.reason: The median is taught here as the middle of an ordered set, and the reason a middle is worth finding is that the values vary. The term is Unit 2 vocabulary carried across several lessons — 2-5 is the lesson that measures variability with range and IQR — rather than instruction 2-3 adds. It moved onto this lesson only because the ORPHAN detector reads the whole config: 2-3's warmup used to be labelled 'Statistical questions and variability', and the warmup now reviews 2-2's histograms instead.

reviewed.subject: Data distribution
reviewed.reason: A box plot is a picture of a distribution — the card says 'how a set of data is spread out' and 'the middle 50%'. The concept is present under plain wording; the term labels it for the unit.

reviewed.subject: Equivalent ratio
reviewed.reason: The card's strategy — 'make one amount the same in both' — is scaling to an equivalent ratio, worked through with 3:5 against 4:7. The method is taught; the noun for it comes from Lesson 3-3.

reviewed.subject: Greater than 100%
reviewed.reason: The key idea states it directly: 'The whole is always 100%, so a percent above 100 means MORE than one whole.' The detector wants the vocabulary entry's exact phrasing; the mathematics is on the card.

reviewed.subject: Equation
reviewed.reason: The card gives the equation as 'part = percent × base' and works 25% of 60 through it. The objective's word for the representation is not repeated, but the representation is the whole card.

reviewed.subject: Edge
reviewed.reason: The content objective calculates volume from fractional edge lengths; the Learn It card works directly with edge measurements in its worked examples.

reviewed.subject: Rational number
reviewed.reason: The key idea says absolute value 'works the same for fractions and decimals as it does for whole numbers', which enumerates the rational numbers the objective names as a category. Same scope, different naming.

reviewed.subject: vertex
reviewed.reason: The card is built on vertex coordinates — 'graph the points, connect them in order' and 'when two vertices share a coordinate' — using corner and vertices rather than the singular the objective states.

reviewed.subject: Perpendicular
reviewed.reason: The x- and y-axes are perpendicular, and that is why reflecting over one changes exactly one coordinate. The card teaches the sign rule; the term names the geometric fact underneath it.

reviewed.subject: Constant
reviewed.reason: Every equation the card writes has one — 'a number of stolen gems plus 8' — and telling the constant from the variable is what makes substitution checkable. Access vocabulary for the equation-writing work.

reviewed.subject: One-step equation
reviewed.reason: Every worked example is a one-step equation solved with one inverse operation: n + 23 = 58. The card teaches the type by doing it rather than by naming the category the objective names.

reviewed.subject: unit rate
reviewed.reason: Unit rate is foundational prerequisite ratio language used in this rates and percentages lesson to connect unit conversions and price comparisons.

reviewed.subject: math biography
reviewed.reason: The card says 'Your math story, one year later' and asks 'how have I changed as a doer of math?'. Biography and story are the same artifact under two names, one in the objective and one on the card.
